category_title: Underprepared writers who utilize non-standard technology like cell phones for long-form academic papers
minimal_context: The student is beginning to draft a 15-page research paper on a social problem during a summer bridge program.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time to start drafting your 15-page research paper on a social problem.

STUDENT: (Pulls out a cell phone and begins typing rapidly with thumbs) I have my topic picked out, so I'll just start writing the draft on here.

TUTOR: Are you planning to write the whole paper on your phone?

STUDENT: Yeah, I’ve never had a computer at home, so I’m used to it.

TUTOR: Do you think that will work for a 15-page assignment?

STUDENT: Definitely. I’m faster on my phone than on a real computer.

options.A: Terminate the writing demands and remove the drafting materials for 10 seconds.
options.B: Lower expectations for the assignment and request two pages instead of fifteen.
options.C: Deliver verbal statements or gestures indicating approval beyond simple acknowledgment.
options.D: Foster learning through a reflective discussion about the drafting process.
